brief.headline: Push for 15-day faster payment in exchange for a small price improvement — we already pay market-fair rates and have four credible backup makers lined up

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 2–3% price cut to land solidly in the typical market band
priceAsk.target: ₹64–65/KG (from current ₹66.48/KG), moving us toward the ₹66–73/kg typical range and closer to the export benchmark of 42.95 ₹/kg
priceAsk.basis: Our ₹66.48/KG is MARKET-FAIR but sits at the top of the ₹66–73/kg typical band; the market ask for Anhydrous Dextrose IP runs ₹60–81/kg, and the India export unit value is 42.95 ₹/kg — a modest cut keeps us competitive and still fair to them

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay 15 days faster (move from 30 days to 15 days after receipt) in return for the price cut
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹61.76 L — paying 15 days sooner frees up this much cash for us, which we trade for a better price

brief.financialLeverage: Sayaji publishes no financials, so we can't gauge how healthy or cash-tight they are. That means we lean on our own data and on having backup sources ready. We spend ₹15.03 Cr a year with them — a meaningful account for any mid-sized dextrose maker. With four qualified alternates (Gulshan Polyols, Sanstar, Tirupati Starch, and Roquette India) and two more public-web leads to check (Gujarat Ambuja, Universal Starch-Chem), we have real negotiating room: we can walk if terms don't improve, but the ask is modest enough that a stable supplier should say yes.

evidence.point: We already pay them the best price in our book for Dextrose
evidence.figure: ₹66.48/KG — same as our best price across all vendors (0.0% gap)

evidence.point: The open-market ask for Anhydrous Dextrose IP is ₹60–81/kg, typically ₹66–73/kg — our price sits at the upper end of 'typical'
India's export unit value for dextrose is materially lower, showing room exists in the market
We spend ₹15.03 Cr annually with Sayaji — large enough to matter
Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹61.76 L of our cash — a concrete trade we can offer
evidence.figure: ₹61.76 L freed if we move to 15-day faster terms

evidence.point: Four qualified backup producers are on file, all making pharma-grade dextrose
evidence.figure: Gulshan Polyols (₹2359.06 Cr revenue, health B 62/100), Sanstar (₹821.13 Cr, C 53/100), Tirupati Starch (₹365.39 Cr, D 27/100), Roquette India (₹2898.05 Cr, D 28/100)

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker with ₹2359.06 Cr revenue and a B (62/100) health score — established dextrose supplier, direct drop-in for Sayaji

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (₹821.13 Cr revenue, C 53/100 health) — growing capacity in starch and dextrose

alternates.name: Roquette India Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Indian arm of global starch major Roquette (₹2898.05 Cr revenue) — pharma-grade dextrose with premium quality systems, very reliable

risks: Sayaji's financials are not public — we can't see cash stress or profit trends, so watch for any signs of supply instability during the meeting
We already pay them our best price (₹66.48/KG, 0.0% gap) — they may resist a cut, arguing they're competitive; counter with the market ask data and the faster-payment offer
Four alternates are qualified, but switching takes time (CoA checks, trial batches) — don't threaten to walk unless you're ready to run a parallel qualification
If they agree to faster payment but no price cut, we lose ₹61.76 L of working cash with no savings — insist the two move together
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to lock in long-term supply and improve our own cash flow — so we're offering to pay you 15 days faster in return for a small price improvement that keeps both of us competitive.
